title: Slap bass and why he gave it up
summary: He brought slap bass from New Orleans to Chicago and California but stopped because it wore grooves in fingerboards and made no notes.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: I finally done that, you understand. I used to have this slap bass business. (Imitating sound of slapping bass fiddle.) I brought that back to Chicago from New Orleans, you know, that slap bass.
Brought it clean on out to California.
But I stopped that because I was wearing out fingerboards.
I had more guts -- not guts. I'm trying to say --
Grooves in my fingerboard, you understand.
And I stopped that. I stopped playing like that. I wouldn't do it no more.
Audiences always love slap bass playing, didn't they?
The people, the folks, liked slap bass playing.
Yeah. Some of it -- (Imitating sound of slapping bass fiddle.) You know. Back with your hand.
So I said, well, you ain't doing nothing there.
Just got a handful of strings and just beating it up against the fingerboard. Ain't making no notes at all.
